r.정치 구도: A 2017 constitutional change abolished the prime minister and created a presidential system concentrating power in the president. President Erdogan has held power for more than 20 years, starting as prime minister, and his Justice and Development Party is the ruling party. Opposition parties such as the Republican People's Party are strong in big-city mayoral races. A failed coup attempt in 2016 was followed by mass purges, and the arrest of Istanbul's mayor in 2025 sparked major protests. Talks to end the long conflict with Kurdish militants are also a major thread in politics.

t.why: It controls the Bosporus and the Dardanelles, the passages linking the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, managing the route for Russian and Ukrainian grain and warships. It has NATO's largest military after the United States, yet bought air defense systems from Russia, causing friction with its allies. It mediated the Ukrainian grain export deal and took in millions of refugees after the Syrian civil war. Its EU accession talks have long been frozen. Exporting many drones, it has emerged as a defense power.
t.rel: A NATO member that also does business with Russia, pursuing an independent foreign policy. It disputes sea boundaries with Greece and Cyprus and confronts Kurdish militants in northern Syria and Iraq militarily.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1957. Because it sent a large force to the Korean War, Koreans call it a 'brother country'. Korean rescuers went after the 2023 earthquake, and Korean builders have built many of its bridges and tunnels, including the Canakkale Bridge. Their free trade agreement took effect in 2013.
t.know: Istanbul straddles two continents, Europe and Asia, on either side of the Bosporus.
etext: A manufacturing base next to Europe

Its customs union with the EU lets it sell lots of cars, appliances and textiles to Europe. Close to Europe with fast transport, it is seen as an ideal place for European companies moving production out of Asia.
It has made a name in the world market with military drones. Turkish construction companies win many big projects in the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa.
Its tourist numbers are among the world's highest. Between Asia and Europe, it is a crossroads for gas pipelines, aviation and logistics.
High inflation and a falling lira have persisted for years. Policy has lurched, forcing interest rates down and then raising them sharply.
